page.layout: One page of running text in a single full-width column. Below the first paragraphs stands a multiplication table in braces, two rows, with the factors and products of each multiplier. Below the table, running text continues to the foot of the page. The catchword "Exem-" stands at the lower right. Running head at the top, page number at the top left. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: rus augmentatur per numerum, & habetur Factus.
Multiplicatio initium sumit à dextra versus sinistram.
Porrò ad unguem te scire oportet multi-plicationem Digitorum: Eamque ex subje-cta tabula facilè discere poteris.

Dicimus autem: bis bina sunt quatuor: bis terna sunt sex: Et contrà, Ter bina sunt sex. Bis quaterna sunt octo: Et contrà, Quater bina sunt octo: Bis quina sunt decem: Et contrà, Quinquies bina sunt decem, &c.

Ex hac tabula discere quoque possunt a-dolescentes quoties numerus in numero contineatur: ut, Novem in octoginta uno continentur Novies: Et Novies Novena sunt 81. 9 autem in 80 continentur 8: Et octies 9 sunt 72: Et 9 in 72 continentur 8: Et octies 9 sunt 72.

page.notes: The multiplication table is a set of braces with factors and products; I have listed one line per box, with the multiplier at level 1 and its factors and products at level 2, in the order printed. The lines of the table are very close together and the exact brace grouping is approximate. The first line of the page is a continuation from the previous page. Some words in the "Dicimus autem" passage are faint (bis terna, quaterna, Quinquies) but are readable. No marginal notes, no footnotes. Long s is transcribed as s throughout.
